diagnosis.root_cause: Fluctuating optical loss on this subscriber's fibre path is driving degraded RX levels and repeated session drops; the ONU laser and authentication state are healthy.
evidence: The current ONU is online and responding, with RX at -27.94 dBm, which is degraded and close to critical; TX at +2.29 dBm is normal.
The seven-day RX series oscillates broadly between approximately -24 and -28.6 dBm while distance remains constant at 302, indicating a changing fibre-path loss rather than a path change.
The series already begins in the degraded RX band, so this is not classified as a declining link; under the stated rule, the session count arbitrates the diagnosis.
There are 16 sessions in 24 hours and the average duration is only 71 minutes, exceeding the 8-session flapping threshold and being far below the 11.9-hour normal duration.
TX power and TX bias current remain stable and healthy, ruling out laser degradation.
All listed peers on EPON0/2 are online with materially better RX levels, so the fault is confined to this customer's path rather than the PON port or shared infrastructure.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, and temperature, and all tested PONs are healthy; the router heartbeat is also healthy.
RADIUS records match CRM, the ONU authentication exchange finishes successfully, and the expected customer VLAN 1092 is present, ruling out authentication and VLAN faults.

remediation.action: Inspect the subscriber drop and its optical connectors/splices, clean and reterminate connectors, and perform OTDR and optical power testing. Repair or replace the degraded fibre segment or passive component if required. Recheck RX stability and session count after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: RX power oscillates between roughly -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle, crossing the threshold at which the link stops being usable. The session drops follow the signal excursions.
expected_reasoning: Sixteen sessions in 24 hours against a 2-3 baseline, with a 71 minute mean duration
Cached RX is -26.28 dBm, already in the degraded band
Telemetry shows RX oscillating between about -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle
The lower excursions cross -28 dBm, at which point the link becomes unusable
Live RX of -27.94 confirms the signal is currently near the bottom of that swing
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable, so the ONU is healthy
RADIUS is clean with a single consistent entry and no mismatches
Peers on EPON0/2 read normal, so the fault is in this customer's own path
The session pattern tracks the signal excursions, so the optical fault explains the flapping
distractors: The trigger names the session count, pointing at the auth layer
Sixteen disconnects is well within the observed flapping tail and could be read as a CPE fault
